kpis.label: $10B EXIM loan + ~$2B private capital; demand-driven stockpile spanning the USGS's full 60-mineral critical list, tied to OEM offtake commitments (GM and others)
NdPr output +41% to 840t, sales more than doubled to 1,006t; adjusted EBITDA turned positive for the first time (reported Aug 6)
Up ~8x since China's Apr-2025 export controls; terbium ~5x, yttrium oxide up to ~140x to ~$1,100/kg — NdPr alloy benchmark alone rose 21.4% in the month to Jul 1
Deal for the only non-Asia mine producing all 4 magnetic rare earths at scale (already in production); shareholder vote Aug 28, 2026

themes.title: Beijing weaponizing processing dominance
themes.description: Ex-China rare-earth prices have exploded since Beijing's April-2025 controls: European dysprosium up ~8x to ~$2,250/kg, terbium ~5x, yttrium oxide up to ~140x to ~$1,100/kg; the NdPr alloy benchmark alone rose 21.4% in the month to Jul 1. Shipments of yttrium, dysprosium and terbium into the US remain down ~50% versus pre-control levels.

themes.title: Truce getting tested
themes.description: Beijing's Jun 22 entity-list additions (MP Materials, USA Rare Earth, among 10 US firms) are testing the fragile Oct-2025 Busan truce, which runs through Nov 10, 2026; analysts are increasingly describing a "rare earth clash 2.0" as tit-for-tat moves resume ahead of the deadline.

themes.title: Washington's playbook
themes.description: Project Vault's $10B EXIM loan + ~$2B private capital remains the umbrella policy, layered with company-level support: DoD's price floor and $140M EBITDA guarantee for MP's 10X plant, USA Rare Earth's $1.6B DoC stake, and Energy Fuels' now-conditional $725M Office of Strategic Capital loan for a terbium/dysprosium build-out.

rows.angle: Only US rare-earth mine + processing (Mountain Pass); $500M Apple magnet offtake (shipments from 2027) + $400M DoD convertible preferred (DoD now largest shareholder, ~15%)
rows.watch for: Q2 2026 (Aug 6): revenue +89% YoY to $108.5M, NdPr output +41% to 840t, adjusted EBITDA positive for the first time; new gadolinium supply deal with a US aerospace/defense customer; 10X magnet plant (2028) carries DoD's ≥$140M EBITDA guarantee at a $110/kg NdPr price floor; capex guidance reaffirmed at $500–600M

rows.angle: Largest non-China rare-earth producer (Australia/Malaysia); pushing into magnet metals
rows.watch for: Record Jun-quarter revenue A$288.9M (+70% YoY), record ASP A$98.2/kg, cash A$1.21B; announced an A$750M equity raise plus a Malaysia magnet-factory partnership to fund "Towards 2030" capacity growth (12,000t NdPr, new A$180M Malaysia HREE plant); shares +7% Aug 5 to A$16.02

Q2 2026 (Aug 6) blew past estimates — adj. EPS $3.75 vs. $3.03 est., EBITDA +155% to $858M as realized lithium prices rose 61%; shares rallied ~11% over two sessions to ~$125. But the print followed an Aug 1 decision to defer hard-rock expansion capex, and China domestic lithium carbonate spot slipped to a ~6-month low (~140,000 CNY/t) the same week

rows.angle: Copper — the electrification metal at scale
rows.watch for: $0.15/share dividend paid Aug 3; Grasberg Block Cave ramp on schedule; FY26 guidance reaffirmed (~$1.90/lb unit cash cost), 2H26 copper sales guided +20% vs. 1H (gold +65%); 2027 copper sales seen up 20%+ vs. 2026, with a potential El Abra (Chile) expansion as further optionality

tiers.label: Developers / Small-Cap — Speculative
tiers.note: Tiered by maturity/risk — not a ranked buy list.

rows.angle: US rare-earth mine-to-magnet aspirant; Texas mine + Oklahoma magnet plant; DoC $1.6B LOI + ~10% equity stake (Jan 2026, priced $17.17)
rows.watch for: Shares jumped ~29% as the Serra Verde tie-up came into focus; DEFM14A filed for the Aug 28 vote on issuing 126.85M new shares ($300M cash + stock; Serra Verde holders end up owning 34.1% of the combined company). Pela Ema (Brazil) is already in production — a real asset, not just a promise — but integration/dilution risk is real; still on China's export-control entity list

rows.angle: Uranium + rare-earth processing at White Mesa
rows.watch for: Q2 2026 (Aug 6): revenue $25.1M, net loss widened to $33.4M (incl. $10.7M in deal costs) while advancing two simultaneous acquisitions (Australian Strategic Materials, VAC) toward a mine-to-magnet platform; White Mesa uranium processing paused for maintenance until Q4 2026/early 2027; the $725M OSC loan remains conditional, not yet closed; ~$1B liquidity

Aug 6: entered a $175M subordinated convertible-debenture agreement with Yorkville Advisors ($150M on 10-Q filing, up to $25M more at LAC's discretion) to shore up Thacker Pass liquidity, layered atop the $2.23B DoE loan (~$435M drawn, DoE holds 5% equity) — a relatively expensive financing structure worth watching

bear_case.title: Commodity cycles cut both ways
bear_case.description: Albemarle's blowout Q2 (lithium prices +61%, EBITDA +155%) came days after it deferred hard-rock expansion capex on Aug 1 — and China's domestic lithium carbonate spot price still slipped to a ~6-month low the same week the results came out. One strong quarter doesn't confirm the cycle has turned.

bear_case.title: China can flood the market
bear_case.description: Beijing has both weaponized scarcity (yttrium oxide up ~140x since the April-2025 controls) and, historically, dumped supply when it suited Beijing's interests; the Nov 10 truce deadline is the key swing factor either way.

bear_case.title: Juniors dilute
bear_case.description: Lithium Americas just layered a $175M Yorkville convertible-debenture facility — a relatively expensive, potentially dilutive structure — on top of its DoE loan; USA Rare Earth is issuing 126.85M new shares (34% of the combined company) to close Serra Verde. Building a rare-earth refinery runs $500M–$1B+, and names without direct sovereign grants keep diluting to get there.

bear_case.title: Policy dependency
bear_case.description: Energy Fuels' $725M OSC loan is still conditional, not closed; the onshoring trade leans on sustained federal appetite and a truce Beijing has already tested once this quarter (Jun 22 entity-list additions). A policy reversal or a durable détente both cut against the thesis, just in different ways.

positions.name: MP Materials
positions.note: Q2 turned adjusted EBITDA positive for the first time (revenue +89% YoY to $108.5M) with Apple's prepayment and DoD's $140M EBITDA guarantee de-risking the 10X ramp. Also appears in Robotics — hold it once, not twice.

positions.name: Freeport-McMoRan
positions.note: Clean quarter: dividend paid, Grasberg Block Cave on schedule, FY26 guidance reaffirmed and 2027 copper sales seen up 20%+ — the least speculative way to own electrification demand.

positions.name: Lynas Rare Earths
positions.note: Record A$288.9M quarter and A$1.21B cash are real, but the new A$750M equity raise for Towards-2030 capacity is a genuine dilution event this week, trimmed slightly to reflect it.

positions.name: USA Rare Earth
positions.note: Serra Verde's Pela Ema mine is already in production, not a promise — a real upgrade to the thesis if the Aug 28 vote passes, but 126.85M new shares (34% of the combined company) is serious dilution risk until then.

positions.name: Energy Fuels
positions.note: Net loss widened to $33.4M while stacking two simultaneous acquisitions (ASM, VAC) on top of a paused White Mesa uranium circuit and a still-conditional $725M loan — trimmed for execution risk.

positions.name: Lithium Americas
positions.note: The $175M Yorkville convertible-debenture facility layered on the DoE loan is a relatively expensive financing structure and a signal of a funding gap at Thacker Pass — trimmed accordingly.

positions.name: Albemarle
positions.note: The Q2 beat (EBITDA +155%, lithium prices +61%) is real, but China domestic lithium carbonate spot hit a ~6-month low the same week — the cycle bottom still isn't confirmed, so this stays a watch, not a hold.
